subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed when `sessions.patch` targets a legacy ownerless session row, requiring operator or non-plugin recovery rather than allowing a plugin to adopt it?
rationale: Ownerless rows provide no trustworthy plugin authority, but rejecting them changes an upgrade path that may have worked before ownership metadata existed; security isolation and compatibility cannot both be inferred safely from code alone.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Keep exact owner equality so a plugin runtime can patch only rows carrying its own `pluginOwnerId`, with operator recovery for legacy rows.

options.title: Add operator-owned migration
options.body: Keep runtime fail-closed behavior but provide a narrow doctor or operator flow to assign or recreate legacy rows safely.

options.title: Preserve ownerless patching
options.body: Allow plugin runtimes to patch ownerless rows for compatibility, accepting that the caller's authority over those rows cannot be established.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Keep exact owner equality so a plugin runtime can patch only rows carrying its own `pluginOwnerId`, with operator recovery for legacy rows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway session lifecycle work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the security-versus-upgrade policy choice.
